title: Home and AI operator
when: Use for planning, explaining the account and initiating a clearly scoped task.
prerequisites: Verified client identity and approved business facts.
steps: Open Home and inspect the current next-action suggestion.
Use a new chat for a distinct job or reopen the relevant chat history.
Describe the desired output, client, audience, facts, constraints and whether the result should remain a draft.
Review the proposed action and any attached assets; distinguish explanation from an executable action.
Check resulting objects in their owning module and record their IDs.
success: The requested artifact exists and its actual state matches the request.
limitations: Chat and recommendation output is fallible; do not let a chat instruction silently authorize spending or delivery.

title: Profile, settings and notifications
when: Use during onboarding, contact changes and preference maintenance.
prerequisites: Correct workspace, approved identity/contact facts and permission to change settings.
steps: Open Settings → Profile; distinguish login email from public contact email.
Fill approved name, business and contact fields and save the profile.
Review agent memory against business facts; amend only relevant entries.
Open Notifications and set only approved push, reply, demand, win-rate and optimization preferences.
Read back changed values and confirm no unintended preference changed.
success: Saved values survive reload; client-facing materials use the correct public details.
limitations: Language selection may save immediately. Reset memory deletes learned context. Auto-Optimize is an operating permission, not just an email preference.

title: Provider and CRM integrations
when: Use before any channel-specific launch, sync, reporting or delivery.
prerequisites: Authorized provider credentials/account access; intended account, page, property, calendar and scope.
steps: Read approval and verification banners before choosing a connection.
Choose the exact integration; follow its OAuth or credential form using the authorized client account.
Verify returned connection state and selected provider IDs.
For CRM, specify sync direction and map fields; test a controlled authorized record before bulk sync.
Check expiry/reconnect behavior and keep secrets outside business knowledge and reports.
success: The required operation works with the intended account; a connected label alone is insufficient.
limitations: Connections may authorize external access. The current account has no ad or delivery integrations; Meta review gating remains.

title: Plans, quotas and billing
when: Use before batching work or evaluating service capacity.
prerequisites: Read-only account access; separate explicit authority for financial changes.
steps: Read plan level and billing status separately.
Check AI credits, Studio usage, intent quota, active campaigns, landing pages, social pages and coaching caps.
Store each reset date; do not combine unlike meters.
Estimate planned usage against the relevant allowance and approved spending ceiling.
Preserve drafts on exhaustion; use a top-up or plan switch only if authorized.
success: The resource plan fits current entitlements and authorized costs.
limitations: Checkout, top-up, cancel, resume and plan-switch operations have financial effects. Partner and customer pricing differ.

title: Brand Kit
when: Use before generating visual assets or after an approved rebrand.
prerequisites: Approved logo, colors, font and style direction.
steps: Open Brand Kit; select the approved logo from the asset library.
Set primary, secondary and accent/background colors.
Select the brand font and describe visual style, desired subjects and exclusions.
Save Brand Kit, reload and confirm the values.
Check the next generated asset actually follows the brand.
success: Saved brand settings and inspected output match the approved identity.
limitations: Applying a brand does not verify facts or rights in generated assets.

title: Veluro Intelligence and business knowledge
when: Use to prepare or update the AI knowledge used across features.
prerequisites: Approved business references and correct isolated account.
steps: Add the main website and specific useful pages.
Upload appropriate supported files within the 30 MB UI limit.
Add structured notes using company, competitor, persona, FAQ, pricing or goal categories.
Inspect knowledge entries and resolve conflicting facts or stale offers.
Ask a bounded factual question and compare the answer with the reference before depending on it.
success: Knowledge entries exist and output accurately reflects the approved source.
limitations: Do not upload passwords, unrelated personal information or another client’s knowledge. Removing an entry changes future AI context.

title: Growth Engine
when: Use to assemble an integrated campaign package around a service and market.
prerequisites: Approved industry/service, offer, market, goal, business knowledge, quotas and delivery plan.
steps: Choose New Growth Engine and select or describe the industry.
Choose the service or services; multiple selections can create multiple engines.
Set market, goal and notes; complete business training inputs.
Create once and record every returned engine ID; poll existing engines rather than restart.
Inspect ads, landing content, outreach, booking and scoring; edit each component.
Before launch, inspect generate-images and publish-landing choices, account routing and authorization.
success: Each component has the expected content and state; live components are independently checked.
limitations: Creation can consume AI resources; launch can publish a page and create media. Live launch was not tested.

title: Ad campaigns and optimization
when: Use to prepare, manage and optimize approved advertising.
prerequisites: Complete client record, provider readiness, approved budget/optimization limits and verified conversion path.
steps: Open New Campaign; use guided setup or the manual builder.
Choose platform, objective, name, lead method and destination.
Configure audience or Google keywords and explicit geography.
Set monthly budget and authorized optimization settings; inspect derived daily budget.
Review creative assets, copy variants, forms/privacy, tracking and nurture.
Save a local draft and read it back; choose paused provider creation or live launch only within authorization.
Poll the existing campaign/job and verify provider IDs, state and delivery before reporting success.
success: Draft read-back or provider state matches the chosen action; spend and conversion events match the client.
limitations: Local drafts are Tested. Live launch, pause, reallocation and autonomous optimization are not production-certified. Scores and simulations are not actual outcomes.

title: High-Intent Buyers and advanced search
when: Use to discover/filter potential buyers and prepare an activation audience.
prerequisites: Approved audience, intended use, geography, topic meaning and lead allowance.
steps: Choose Business buyers, Consumers or filter-only Advanced search.
For intent, search at least three characters and pick up to five relevant topic IDs; avoid irrelevant named-company matches.
Apply recency, state/city/ZIP and appropriate B2B or B2C filters.
Name the tracker and review its allocation before building; the observed default is large.
Record audience ID and poll until complete; inspect counts, sample quality and applied filters.
Export or activate only the intended audience, verifying provider match, CRM mapping and delivery authorization.
success: The returned list matches intended filters and its source/quality are understood.
limitations: No audience generation/export or match-rate test was run. Deletion releases quota next cycle. Advanced search is not intent evidence.

title: Pixels and conversion tracking
when: Use before measuring or optimizing campaign conversion events.
prerequisites: Authorized site/funnel access and correct provider tag/pixel ID.
steps: Open Add Pixel and choose Meta, Google, LinkedIn, TikTok or Custom Script.
Enter the actual provider identifier/script and a descriptive name.
Generate and inspect install code; assign it only to the intended page/funnel.
Install through the authorized site flow and trigger a controlled test conversion.
Verify the event in the provider and ensure events are not double-fired.
success: Actual provider event receipt and intended page placement are verified.
limitations: Creating a Veluro pixel record is not proof of installation. Custom scripts execute on client pages.

title: Sales funnels and funnel editor
when: Use for a multi-step conversion, booking or sales flow.
prerequisites: Approved offer, audience, CTA, brand, tracking and any payment/automation authorization.
steps: Create Funnel and choose AI or template.
For AI, specify goal, product/offer, audience, market, desired outcome and style.
Record the funnel ID and wait for generation; inspect each page and step.
Edit content, forms, step order and upsell/downsell paths; verify navigation and conversion mapping.
Configure only approved pixels, automations, payment connection and webhooks.
Preview responsive output; publish only on the approved destination; verify actual submissions.
success: The served flow, routing, forms and authorized downstream actions work end to end.
limitations: Template creation can create stored objects. Automation test buttons can send real messages. Payment, publishing and variant promotion were not executed.

title: Landing pages and A/B tests
when: Use for a single conversion-focused page and controlled variants.
prerequisites: Approved business description, CTA, branding, domain, privacy and page allowance.
steps: Supply business name, detailed offer and CTA goal.
Optionally extract design from an inspiration URL; review design use and write original client copy.
Choose look/feel and generate once; preserve page ID.
Edit sections, images, form and CTA; preview desktop/mobile output.
Publish to the approved slug/domain and verify domain status and served content.
For A/B tests, record variant IDs, metric and evaluation window before promoting a winner.
success: The actual page and conversion destination work, and variant decisions use real data.
limitations: Generation, saving, publishing, domain verification and autopilot are separate operations. Page creation is quota-limited.

title: Demand Map and surge alerts
when: Use for market research and geographically focused campaign planning.
prerequisites: Approved operating geography, service categories and an interpretable source of demand.
steps: Enter a specific city/state/region; remove irrelevant default categories.
Optionally select the intended saved audience.
Generate the map once and inspect location, segments, estimated volumes and assumptions.
Drill into a hotspot before creating a campaign; verify target geography in the campaign itself.
Enable email surge alerts only under the client’s notification preference.
success: Map interpretation and resulting campaign geography are reviewed and recorded.
limitations: Estimated demand is not a census. The source request supplies descriptive audience context; exact person-level targeting is unverified.

title: SEO audit and rank tracking
when: Use to diagnose site issues and track approved keywords.
prerequisites: Correct website, site editing authority and relevant keywords/competitors.
steps: Run a site audit against the intended URL.
Inspect findings and proposed fixes; verify issues on the actual pages.
Set keywords, competitor and scan preferences deliberately.
Apply approved changes in the website system and rerun relevant checks.
Compare rank history using the same terms, location and time window.
success: Actual site changes and tracked observations support the reported improvement.
limitations: An audit score or generated fix is not proof of ranking improvement. Repeated scans may consume resources.

title: SEO Blog Engine
when: Use for source-backed organic content and an approved business blog.
prerequisites: Approved topic, sources, brand voice and publishing destination.
steps: Choose a primary topic/keyword or request topic suggestions.
Generate one article and record the post ID.
Review claims, links, metadata, FAQ schema and quotations; edit to match client evidence.
Preview and publish only the approved version to the intended blog.
Verify served URL and content; use unpublish when an authorized rollback is needed.
success: The published article is accurate, correctly branded and reachable at the expected URL.
limitations: AI readiness and SEO scores are heuristics. Publishing and unpublishing are external actions.

title: GEO and AI visibility
when: Use for testing brand visibility in AI answers and preparing structured content.
prerequisites: Correct brand, website, competitors and representative buyer prompts.
steps: Set brand/website/competitors and review the generated buyer prompts.
Run the scan and poll its ID to completion.
Inspect the tested prompts, returned answers and scoring rather than rely only on a score.
Run the site audit; generate llms.txt or FAQ JSON-LD as drafts.
Review facts and schema; deploy only through approved site access, then verify served content.
success: The report clearly distinguishes observed answers from predicted future visibility.
limitations: GEO settings can save during editing. Files and scores do not guarantee mentions or ranking.

title: Local Listings
when: Use to check availability of the planned Google Business Profile feature.
prerequisites: Current feature availability.
steps: Open Local Listings and inspect its state.
If it still says Coming Soon, record unavailable and continue other work.
When released, verify actual GBP connection, location selection and approved edit/review-reply workflows before use.
success: Availability is reported accurately.
limitations: Coming Soon in the inspected account. Do not claim listing management or review response works here.

title: Leads CRM and imports
when: Use to maintain the authorized client pipeline and route follow-up.
prerequisites: Approved source data, contact permissions, deduplication rules and CRM field mapping.
steps: Inspect table/pipeline, status/campaign/score filters and grouping.
Add a lead with email or phone, or import the authorized CSV through the file chooser.
Validate field mapping, imported/skipped counts and duplicate handling.
Review lead score and status using actual contact history.
Enroll only eligible contacts into the approved sequence; verify delivery logs and synchronization.
success: The intended records and counts match source data without unintended enrollment or duplicates.
limitations: Import and sync mutate the CRM. Custom-status read returned 404 in this account; validate before relying on custom stages.

title: Nurture Campaigns
when: Use for approved follow-up to eligible leads.
prerequisites: Reviewed sequence, eligible enrolled leads, sender route, Twilio for SMS and stop/suppression rules.
steps: Inspect campaign statuses and enrolled leads.
Review each step’s channel, delay, subject and body.
Confirm email and SMS delivery connections separately.
Activate/send only under the approved outreach scope.
Inspect delivery, replies and failures; stop or suppress leads according to the client rules.
success: Actual delivery and enrollment states match the approved sequence.
limitations: The visible activation API is activate-send. Emails/SMS can remain queued without the corresponding connection.

title: Replies Inbox
when: Use to triage responses to the client’s campaigns.
prerequisites: Correct client inbox and response authorization.
steps: Read the relevant replies and originating lead/campaign.
Identify intent, requested action, opt-out or delivery issue.
Update the lead and stop/suppress further follow-up where appropriate.
Prepare a contextual response and send only if the engagement authorizes it.
Verify reply/delivery state and record the next step.
success: The reply is handled with accurate context and no conflicting automated follow-up.
limitations: Opening a reply may mark it read. Reply generation and sending are different effects.

title: Email Triage and connected inbox
when: Use for authorized inbox management and reply preparation.
prerequisites: The intended email account is connected and in scope.
steps: Connect the specific mailbox through the supported account flow.
Inspect only the requested folders/messages.
Run triage when authorized and review classifications and proposed drafts.
Approve or send the correct response within engagement scope.
Verify message state; distinguish star, archive, delete and send actions.
success: The intended email is handled and its resulting state is checked.
limitations: The inspected account had no email connection. This is separate from cold outreach sender setup.

title: AI Reply Drafter
when: Use to prepare a response from provided email text.
prerequisites: Relevant email, accurate business context and desired outcome.
steps: Paste the email into the drafter.
Choose the intended outcome and provide needed context.
Generate, review and refine for factual accuracy and tone.
Copy the result into the authorized sending surface or preserve as a draft.
Check history only within the correct client account.
success: A usable reviewed draft is produced; delivery is claimed only if separately verified.
limitations: Do not treat reassuring privacy copy in the UI as a verified server retention guarantee.

title: LinkedIn prospecting, Compose and queue
when: Use for B2B prospect records, manually sent copy and reminder sequences.
prerequisites: Approved prospect context and intended LinkedIn workflow.
steps: Add the prospect with accurate name/company/profile.
Choose Compose and provide role, industry, hook and relevant context.
Generate connection request, InMail, follow-up or reply copy.
Review and preserve copy; the built-in Compose feature does not send it.
Save a sequence to the Outreach Queue when appropriate; mark sent only after actual authorized sending elsewhere.
success: Prospect records, copy and reminders reflect actual work and message history.
limitations: Marketing API connection, identity login and Compose are different capabilities. Do not automate DM delivery by inference.

title: CSV email campaigns and sender setup
when: Use for approved list-based email programs.
prerequisites: Authorized list, verified sender setup, suppression, send window and provider cost allowance.
steps: Configure the intended mailbox or Resend sender and verify connection/route.
Import the CSV and validate list count/mapping and suppression.
Create campaign with purpose, value proposition, tone, sequence length and CTA.
Inspect all messages and sender routing; set launch timing deliberately.
Launch only within approved audience/sending scope; monitor delivery, replies, bounces and opt-outs.
Pause and reconcile before retrying any ambiguous send operation.
success: Correct recipients receive the intended messages and suppression/reply behavior is verified.
limitations: Current Lists/Campaigns tabs were gated by absent senders. Source exposes mailbox warmup and test-send actions, which can send real messages.

title: Scheduling and calendar
when: Use to offer slots, book meetings and maintain authorized calendars.
prerequisites: Correct calendar, timezone, availability, contact and invitation authorization.
steps: Select the intended day and inspect available slots.
Set title, time, duration, contact and notes.
Check conflicts and the calendar integration before confirming.
Create the appointment only within invitation scope.
Verify the actual calendar event, booking state and public reschedule/cancel path when used.
success: The right people have the correct event in the intended timezone and calendar.
limitations: Scheduling may send invites or sync externally. No connected calendar workflow was tested.

title: Proposals and signatures
when: Use to prepare and deliver approved commercial proposals.
prerequisites: Accurate client identity/email, authorized prices/terms and signing process.
steps: Open New Proposal or an approved template.
Fill client, company, validity date, title, introduction, sections and line items.
Review totals, notes, scope and AI-drafted language against approved terms.
Save and inspect PDF output.
Send for Signature only after final scope authorization; verify the intended recipient and signature state.
success: The saved/exported proposal is correct; signing events are supported by the audit record.
limitations: AI Draft, Save, PDF and Send for Signature are distinct. Do not invent signature, agreement or pricing.

title: AI Sales Coach
when: Use before, during and after authorized sales calls.
prerequisites: Approved playbook, accurate prospect context, available seat/call/minute quota and recording process.
steps: Select the appropriate playbook and prepare prospect/company/pain/goal/objections.
Generate prep and check that advice fits the offer.
For Live, arm only when the agreed recording process permits; verify microphone capture.
For Review, paste transcript or upload authorized audio and inspect analysis.
Review drafted follow-up before any send; reconcile usage and maintain session history.
success: Useful coaching is grounded in the actual call, and usage/session records are verified.
limitations: UI exposes 10 analyses / 300 minutes in this plan, plus one seat. Live microphone capture and analysis were not run.

title: Website chat widgets
when: Use to answer website questions and capture eligible leads.
prerequisites: Approved bot identity, business knowledge, privacy process, embed access and CRM routing.
steps: Create a widget with name, welcome, color, goal and tone.
Supply business/services/FAQ and optional website/files.
Inspect knowledge ingestion; test common questions and unsafe/unknown cases in simulation.
Review appearance, lead fields and booking destination.
Embed only on the approved site, then verify real capture and CRM routing.
success: The actual embedded widget answers accurately and records leads in the correct account.
limitations: Simulation may use AI credits. Widget creation, toggle, duplicate and embed are separate actions.

title: Social Media Manager and autopilot
when: Use to prepare and publish an approved social content calendar.
prerequisites: Correct profiles/pages, brand assets, approved content and schedule/timezone.
steps: Check each platform connection and current approval gates.
Create a manual post or generate a strategy/batch for review.
Inspect text, links, hashtags and finished image/video for each platform.
Save drafts or approve/schedule within the agreed publishing scope.
Verify provider publication and calendar state; reconcile before retrying failures.
Configure autopilot only with explicit content, frequency and spending limits.
success: Posts appear on the intended profile at the intended time with correct content.
limitations: Dragging a post can reschedule it. Autopilot can create and publish content; general Meta approval remains gated.

title: Creative Studio
when: Use to generate image/video assets or assemble creative variants.
prerequisites: Approved creative brief, asset rights, exact model variant, credit allowance and output specs.
steps: Choose Guided or Pro mode and the intended output type.
Read current model slug, price, ratio/duration and reference-image requirements.
Write the brief and inspect added text/branding fields.
Generate once and store the job/generation ID; poll rather than resubmit.
Review finished output and saved library asset, then check credit delta.
Use Photos → Video, Ad Lab or storyboard only for the matching need and inspect their separate final actions.
success: The finished asset meets specification, exists in the library and has a verified cost/result.
limitations: Model names can repeat with different costs. Avatar/audio labels do not establish available models. Generation was not executed.

title: Storyboard Video Builder
when: Use for a multi-scene video assembled from a script.
prerequisites: Approved script, duration, aspect ratio, scene plan and credit ceiling.
steps: Supply the script/brief and select 15/30/45/60 seconds and ratio.
Build the storyboard; preserve project and scene IDs.
Review script and each scene before generation.
Generate required clips, poll their existing IDs and check each result.
Stitch only complete approved clips; inspect final video/audio and library output.
success: The final stitched video matches the approved scene order and technical specification.
limitations: Generating scenes and stitching are distinct jobs; partial completion must not trigger duplicate generation.

title: Creative Library and asset editing
when: Use to organize, upload, reuse and edit approved assets.
prerequisites: Correct client assets, rights and intended output.
steps: Filter Social, Ads, AI Creatives or Media Library.
Import image/video only when needed; record asset IDs and folder.
Open the appropriate image/video editor and preserve an original.
Apply approved edits, resizing, background removal or video changes; poll render jobs.
Inspect exported media and use the correct asset ID in campaigns/posts.
success: The intended asset and edited/exported version are identifiable and usable.
limitations: Delete, AI edit, folder assignment and launch-as-ads have different effects. Do not infer that a thumbnail is a finished render.

title: Creative Insights
when: Use to analyze actual ad creative performance.
prerequisites: Connected correct Meta account and reliable date-window metrics.
steps: Connect the intended account and select the date range.
Inspect ad-level results and underlying provider metrics.
Ask a bounded analytical question tied to the selected ads.
Compare suggested tests with the actual winning/losing evidence.
Prepare revised assets as drafts; execute budget or live creative changes only within authority.
success: Recommendations can be traced to the actual ads and reporting window.
limitations: The current account is gated by absent Meta connection. Fatigue and AI scores do not replace observed results.

title: Flyers and PDF output
when: Use for an approved printable promotional artifact.
prerequisites: Approved business/offer/contact details, branding and image rights.
steps: Fill name, headline, subheadline, offer, CTA, phone, website and QR URL.
Choose a design and approved image; review AI-generated copy if used.
Save the flyer and inspect the preview.
Download PDF and verify text fit, page layout and QR/phone/link accuracy.
Preserve the final approved PDF with the client record.
success: The printable artifact is accurate, readable and has working destinations.
limitations: Save and generation differ from PDF export. Do not use unverified performance claims in the offer.

title: Dashboard, analytics and reports
when: Use to review actual operations and produce evidence-backed reporting.
prerequisites: Correct data sources, dates, timezone, attribution and currency.
steps: Choose Overview, Analytics, Command Center or Reports.
Read empty/disconnected states explicitly and verify underlying sources.
Inspect consistent date windows before comparing metrics.
Generate insights/report only when its inputs are understood.
Review numbers, forecasts and recommendations; export/share only the verified report.
success: Reported results reconcile to source events and the stated window.
limitations: A Live label, chart, generated insight or PDF is not proof of real underlying business activity.

title: Business Health and reputation
when: Use only after verifying the origins of the business and financial data.
prerequisites: Reconciled source metrics; approved action scope.
steps: Inspect health components and their underlying details.
Check connected sources and reconcile revenue, spend, conversion, retention and reputation against them.
Flag unexplained/sample figures and exclude them from client decisions.
Review any recommendation with its actual evidence and expected effect.
Execute an action only after provenance and authorization are established; read back actual outcomes.
success: Scores and proposed actions have demonstrated data lineage.
limitations: Current account has a material provenance conflict. Do not use its populated metrics to trigger spending, financial actions or messaging.

title: Competitor Tracking
when: Use to track relevant public competitor activity and inform approved tests.
prerequisites: Correct competitors, official sites and a defined comparison question.
steps: Add a competitor or review AI suggestions.
Verify company name and website before saving.
Run analysis and inspect cited/current evidence.
Separate observation from inference and unsupported positioning claims.
Use findings to prepare an approved test and record source date.
success: Competitive claims are supported by the right company/source and date.
limitations: Analysis can be incomplete or stale. Do not copy unsupported statistics into outreach.

title: Weekly Digest
when: Use for a reviewed weekly operating summary.
prerequisites: Verified data and a defined reporting period; permission for email delivery if used.
steps: Read an existing digest or generate the first.
Compare figures with source records and annotate missing data.
Review optimization recommendations against approved goals.
Preserve the reviewed digest and next actions.
Send via Email only if delivery is authorized; verify intended recipient and delivery result.
success: The summary is accurate and delivered only through the intended channel.
limitations: Generate and Send via Email are separate operations; no digest email was sent.

title: Client workspace team and roles
when: Use to provision or audit operator access in the client application.
prerequisites: Owner/admin scope and approved person/role.
steps: Read the actual role matrix and current member list.
Choose Owner/Admin/Member according to the required tasks.
Prepare the specific invite or role change; verify the exact email/person.
Send or save only when member-management authorization covers it.
Verify membership status and that only intended permissions changed.
success: The right operator has the required access in the correct client workspace.
limitations: Member cannot run AI agents in the displayed matrix. Only Owner can manage billing/settings. Invites send external messages.

title: Partner dashboard, resellers and payouts
when: Use for referral tracking, recruitment attribution and partner staff operations.
prerequisites: Correct partner account, referral code and agreement.
steps: Use Overview for referred customers and settled/pending commissions.
Use My Team for recruited resellers and Team Members for staff; do not conflate them.
Use the appropriate main, trial or reseller invite link and preserve tracking.
Use the calculator with 20% direct, 10% reseller subscription and 5% reseller-client revenue bases.
Inspect payout/clearing records; verify actual payout separately from projected commission.
Prepare staff/income/link changes deliberately and perform them only within scope.
success: Attribution, commission base, staff relationship and actual payout states are accurately recorded.
limitations: Payout/bank changes and invitations require the appropriate authority. No recruitment message or payout action was performed.

title: Marketing Library and Starter Kit
when: Use to prepare Veluro promotional materials with the correct referral attribution.
prerequisites: Approved offer, actual commission terms and permission for any publication/advertising.
steps: Choose the Veluro asset group and inspect the material’s intended channel.
Check the referral URL and any per-asset attribution parameters.
Adapt text and fact-check statistics, trial claims and feature promises.
Download/copy a reviewed asset or prepare a campaign draft.
Launch/share only within the approved promotional scope and inspect performance attribution.
success: The material contains accurate claims and the correct tracked link; actual publishing is independently verified.
limitations: Prebuilt launch buttons can create ads. Investment-related asset groups were outside this Veluro documentation scope.

title: Help, guides and support
when: Use to learn setup or resolve a discrepancy.
prerequisites: Current live UI and dated evidence.
steps: Search Help or choose its category.
Open the relevant guide and compare labels/limits with the live page.
Follow verified current controls rather than stale illustrations.
Record any discrepancy in the verification register and continue independent work.
Prepare a precise support question with sanitized evidence if needed; do not send without messaging authority.
success: Instructions match the current usable interface and unresolved gaps are explicit.
limitations: The built-in guides have some stale labels and topic limits; vendor descriptions are not execution proof.
